causal_assessment.java_model: CommandFactoryNote.singleLine uses [%g] then ([^%g]+) then [%g]; Pattern2 expands %g to ASCII double quote, U+201C, U+201D, and Jaws.BLOCK_E1_INVISIBLE_QUOTE U+E121. Each boundary is independently any member. An embedded member ends DISPLAY, and a nonconforming remainder leaves no command candidate. PSystemCommandFactory then returns a syntax error instead of consuming later lines.
causal_assessment.jaws_assessment: Jaws defines U+E121 and expands Jaws text blocks with the same marker. The raw-U+E121 held-outs prove the Java JAR and frozen Rust binary both receive this Pattern2 delimiter case.
causal_assessment.rust_model: parse_named_note_inline correctly uses the four-member quote class for a fully valid command. looks_like_named_note_inline_command repeats that full delimiter grammar before terminal rejection. When an embedded %g member occurs before the delimiter that precedes 'as', its non-quote run cannot cross the member and the early candidate is not followed by whitespace plus 'as'; the ownership predicate returns false. Component and Deployment therefore fall through to their relation parsers, which synthesize endpoints.
causal_assessment.conclusion: The correction fixes valid curly, mixed, and Jaws delimiters but does not model the terminal rejection of malformed lines whose DISPLAY is cut short by an embedded %g member.

findings.title: Embedded Pattern2 delimiters still escape terminal named-note ownership
findings.java_provenance: CommandFactoryNote.singleLine's DISPLAY is [^%g]+. Pattern2 includes U+201C and U+E121 in %g, so each held-out is a Java syntax error and PSystemCommandFactory stops before relation execution.
findings.rust_data_flow: parse_named_note_inline returns None for the malformed command. looks_like_named_note_inline_command also returns false because its non-quote run cannot cross the embedded delimiter and the early delimiter is not immediately followed by 'as'. Component then reaches its RE_DESCRIPTION_CONN endpoint synthesis; Deployment reaches try_parse_connection endpoint synthesis.
findings.impact: Both failures violate the corrected claimed invariant: an invalid CommandFactoryNote-shaped line allows later source to mutate the AST.

findings.title: The corrected four-member delimiter model works for valid forms
findings.detail: Ten fresh valid probes cover Component and Deployment, ASCII/left/right/U+E121 delimiters, same and asymmetric pairs, case/NBSP whitespace, root/nested ownership, Unicode dotted codes, escaped-newline displays, tags, stereotypes, colors, and later relations. Each is accepted by Java and the frozen Rust binary.

findings.title: Ordinary invalid suffixes terminate before endpoint synthesis
findings.detail: Empty display, malformed code, reordered decorations, unknown color, and malformed multiline forms all produce Java error SVGs and frozen-Rust parse failures. The failure is limited to the embedded-delimiter ownership boundary.

declared_residue_assessment: Deployment note-on-link is preserved as a separate known defect and is explicitly excluded from this mechanism's acceptance and verdict.
The unforced Deployment link-note control selected the State parser; it is preserved as a top-level subtype-selection observation and is not counted as Deployment evidence.
Java and Rust error-page SVG artwork, diagnostics, and line numbers are not compared; Java-valid acceptance/rejection and frozen AST mutation are the oracle for this review.
verdict_reason: REJECT. The correction accepts valid Pattern2 delimiter combinations, but two fresh malformed inputs with embedded %g members are rejected by the exact Java oracle and accepted by frozen Rust. In both Component and Deployment, the named-note ownership predicate fails to claim the malformed line, and a later relation synthesizes the would-be note code. The failures are preserved and executable under the followup perturbation directory.
